title: The Full Picture

patient.name: Mdm Halimah binte Yusof
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient registering for an eye clinic visit; needs a general health, medication and allergy history

history.hpc: Mdm Halimah is a new patient. The PSA must take a general health history. She initially mentions only diabetes, then on prompting adds: 'Oh, I also take the blood-thinner one, and sometimes herbal jamu from my neighbour. And one time the nurse gave me an eye drop, my eye became very itchy and swollen.' Capturing systemic conditions, all medications, and allergies is essential for safe care.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, atrial fibrillation (on anticoagulant).
history.social_hx: Lives with family. Takes traditional supplements occasionally.

investigations.history_documentation: Structured general health history obtained: systemic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, AF), all medications including the anticoagulant and herbal supplement, and a clear drug allergy (previous reaction to an eye drop). Family history of glaucoma noted. The allergy is flagged prominently.

diagnosis: A thorough general health, medication, and allergy history for a new patient uncovers an anticoagulant, a herbal supplement, and an eye-drop allergy — all important for safe care and any future procedure. This case is about complete, safe history taking; clinical decisions are the doctor's.

immediate: Take a structured general health history: systemic conditions, all medications, allergies
Specifically ask about blood thinners (anticoagulants), herbal supplements, and vitamins, which are often omitted
Elicit and prominently flag the drug allergy (previous eye-drop reaction)
Note the family history of glaucoma
Measure VA and document the full history clearly for the doctor
Ensure the allergy is recorded so the offending drop is not given
follow_up: Doctor to factor the anticoagulant into any planned procedure/surgery
Advise the patient to bring a list of all medicines and supplements to future visits
Confirm the specific herbal supplement where possible
patient_education: Explain that blood thinners, herbal supplements, and allergies are important for safe treatment
Reassure her that sharing this keeps her safe
Advise keeping an up-to-date medication list
Explain the allergy will be flagged so she is not given that drop again

key_points: Takes a structured general health and medication history
Specifically probes for anticoagulants, herbal supplements, and vitamins
Elicits and records the eye-drop allergy
Documents all systemic conditions and the full medication list
Records the history completely for the doctor
Recognises the anticoagulant as important for any future procedure
Understands why herbal supplements must be elicited
Identifies the eye-drop allergy as a key safety item
Frames the task as complete, safe history taking
Documents medications, supplements, and allergy accurately
Ensures the allergy is flagged in the record
Educates the patient on why these details matter
Advises bringing an updated medication list to future visits
